source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 4 defines a finite-sample neural partial-identification estimator and proves an almost-sure asymptotic bracket under assumptions involving latent c-components; Corollary 2's nonasymptotic ATE rate additionally assumes no confounding.
Definition 2.3 defines canonical SCMs with finite endogenous and exogenous domains, and Theorem 2.4 preserves all counterfactual distributions for an arbitrary SCM with the same causal diagram.

The published paper reduces discrete causal questions to polynomial programs and supplies dual-relaxation/spatial-branch-and-bound outer bounds with continually refined non-sharp ranges and epsilon-sharpness.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 1, abstract; pp. 2–3, SCM setup and definitions
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper treats implicit generative models with continuous and discrete variables, proves tight convergence for linear SCMs, and presents nonlinear results empirically rather than exact-feasibility neural certificates.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add measurability of kappa to the full-class setup; for the certificate theorem require alpha to be rational and give an explicit finite semialgebraic representation of C_n and the coded-law constraints, including how required cell integrals are represented or bounded.

Replace every broad statement that Tan et al. lack finite-sample latent-confounded guarantees with the precise comparison: their finite-sample-defined estimator has asymptotic consistency, but no exact finite-sample confidence region covering the whole coded-law identified set.

Strengthen the certification contribution with a worked nontrivial mixed-variable ADMG certificate, including checker input, certificate size, and verified endpoint gap; this would make the grammar boundary and distinct trust advance concrete.

recommended_next_step: Revise the measurability and rational-semialgebraic certificate contract, correct the Tan comparison, then advance the repaired field-tier lifting/certification kernel to Stage 0.
